chapter: Career overview and the Lunceford quarrel
title: Bill Robinson tells Lunceford to pay him off
summary: In a theater, Bill Robinson's valet gives Lunceford money to pay off Crawford with a racial slur, and Crawford still resents Robinson.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: So I just got filled up, and Bill Robinson in some theater, now -- I can't recall what theater we were in -- this man, after he heard me out there telling Lunsford off -- and I'm telling the God's truth -- he gave his -- told his valet, name was Billy, give me some money, give me some money. So he came out and told Lunsford, here -- wonder can I use this word I'm going to use.
Oh, you can use any word you want to. I hope they erase it

All right (inaudible), which I don't like that word myself, and I don't like the word hate, I say I dislike. So he says, here, here, Jimmie. Pay that nigger off over there and let him go; turn him loose. Who needs him?

Now, this man had no business saying that. He wasn't any part of Lunsford's band. He was just a featured actor, buck dancer, I called him. He's dead now. Soon as I get a chance, I'm going to throw another shovel of dirt in his face, on his grave.

I disliked that man so much, until I'm going to use the word hate. He didn't have any business butting in Lunsford's business. Lunsford politely told him, said, now, let him alone, let him alone. I'll take care of that. Say, we're together; we started out together. We're going to stay together as long as he want to stay here.
